newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kashmiris in Pakistan protest peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiris in Pakistan protest peace talks.

text.p: Protesters took to the streets in a Pakistan-ruled section of the disputed Kashmir region on Friday to protest India-Pakistan peace talks now taking place in New Delhi.

Dozens of Kashmiris marched to the office of a U.N. military observers group at Muzaffarabad, capital of the Pakistani Azad (free) Kashmir, shouting slogans including "we want freedom" and "wake up United Nations".
About 100 Kashmiri activists paraded in Muzaffarabad in a separate protest against the talks, which resumed in New Delhi on Friday after being stalled for more than three years.
"The Indo-Pakistan talks without Kashmiris is a futile exercise," a local leader of the umbrella All Parties Hurriyat (freedom) Conference group, Mushtaq Wani, told reporters.
He said Kashmiris must be made a party to any talks between India and Pakistan, which have fought two of their three wars since independence from Britain in 1947 over Kashmir.
Hurriyat groups some 30 organizations that oppose Indian rule over two-thirds of Kashmir. The remaining third is controlled by Pakistan.
